curriculum.lesson_evidence: Red, yellow and blue are the primary colours in paint. You cannot make them by mixing other paint colours. Mixing two primaries makes a secondary colour: red and yellow make orange, yellow and blue make green, and blue and red make purple. Adding white makes a lighter tint and adding a tiny amount of a dark colour makes a darker shade. Add small amounts of the darker colour a little at a time, because it is strong.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
You have only red, yellow, blue and white paint. How would you make a bright orange for a pumpkin and a pale purple for a flower? Write the colours you would mix and the amounts in parts.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: orange is red and yellow, for example 1 red + 2 yellow so it is not too red. Pale purple is blue and red mixed, then white added a little at a time. Writing the parts means you can make the same colour again.

WATCH FOR
Thinking that mixing more colours always gives a better colour. Mixing all three primaries together makes a dull brown or grey, so artists mix only what they need and test on scrap paper first.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Make a colour wheel with the three primary colours and three secondary colours using paint, crayons or coloured pencils. Under each secondary colour write its recipe. Then mix one tint and one shade of your favourite colour and name each.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example: Ana wants a leaf green. She puts yellow on her palette first, then adds a small dab of blue. The mix is bright green. For a darker green for shadows she adds a bit more blue. For a pale spring green she adds white. She wrote the recipe: 3 yellow + 1 blue = light green.

TRY FIRST
You have only red, yellow, blue and white paint. How would you make a bright orange for a pumpkin and a pale purple for a flower? Write the colours you would mix and the amounts in parts.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: orange is red and yellow, for example 1 red + 2 yellow so it is not too red. Pale purple is blue and red mixed, then white added a little at a time. Writing the parts means you can make the same colour again.
teach_steps.explain:
Red, yellow and blue are the primary colours in paint. You cannot make them by mixing other paint colours. Mixing two primaries makes a secondary colour: red and yellow make orange, yellow and blue make green, and blue and red make purple. Adding white makes a lighter tint and adding a tiny amount of a dark colour makes a darker shade. Add small amounts of the darker colour a little at a time, because it is strong.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the elements, techniques or performance choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. One deliberate artistic choice with a named effect is more useful than a longer praise sentence.
